# Test BlockForest 

```{r}
library(blockForest)
```

```{r}
# NOTE: There is no association between covariates and response for the
# simulated data below.
# Moreover, the input parameters of blockfor() are highly unrealistic
# (e.g., nsets = 10 is specified much too small).
# The purpose of the shown examples is merely to illustrate the
# application of predict.blockForest().


# Generate data:
################

set.seed(1234)

# Covariate matrix:
X <- cbind(matrix(nrow=40, ncol=5, data=abs(rnorm(40*5))), 
           matrix(nrow=40, ncol=30, data=abs(rnorm(40*30, mean=1, sd=2))),
           matrix(nrow=40, ncol=100, data=abs(rnorm(40*100, mean=2, sd=3))))
colnames(X) <- paste("X", 1:ncol(X), sep="")

# Block variable (list):
block <- rep(1:3, times=c(5, 30, 100))
block <- lapply(1:3, function(x) which(block==x))

# Survival outcome:
ysurv <- cbind(abs(rnorm(40)), sample(c(0,1), size=40, replace=TRUE))


# Divide in training and test data:
Xtrain <- X[1:30,]
Xtest <- X[31:40,]

ysurvtrain <- ysurv[1:30,]
ysurvtest <- ysurv[31:40,]


# Survival outcome: Apply algorithm to training data and obtain predictions
# for the test data:
###########################################################################

# Apply a variant to the training data:

blockforobj <- blockfor(Xtrain, ysurvtrain, num.trees = 100, replace = TRUE, blocks=block,
                        nsets = 100, num.trees.pre = 50, splitrule="extratrees", 
                        block.method = "BlockForest")

blockforobj$paramvalues
blockforobj$biased_oob_error_donotuse

blockforobj$forest$forest
  
  # Obtain prediction for the test data:

(predres <- predict(blockforobj$forest, data = Xtest))


predres$chf
predres$survival
predres$unique.death.times

rowSums(predres$chf)
```


```{r}
library(survival)
concordance_index <- concordance(Surv(ysurvtest[,1], ysurvtest[,2]) ~ rowSums(predres$chf), timewt = "n/G2") #Unos C

concordance_index

coef(concordance_index)
concordance_index$concordance
concordance_index$var
```

```{r}
library(SurvMetrics)

# Define time of interest
## Option 1: Use times of actual events in test data
IBSrange <- sort(ysurvtest[,1][ysurvtest[,2] == 1])

## Option 2: Generate 100 uniformly spaced points within the time range (min, 0.9 quantile) of the test data
IBSrange <- seq(min(ysurvtest[,1]), quantile(ysurvtest[,1], 0.9), length.out = 100)

SurvMetrics::IBS(Surv(ysurvtest[,1], ysurvtest[,2]), predres$survival, IBSrange = c(IBSrange))
```






```{r}
library(survival)
# Create risk groups based on cumulative hazard estimates
risk_group <- ifelse(rowSums(predres$chf) > median(rowSums(predres$chf)), "high", "low")

surv_test <- survdiff(Surv(ysurvtest[,1], ysurvtest[,2]) ~ risk_group)
surv_test
```

```{r}
out_df <- as.data.frame(ysurvtest) %>% rownames_to_column("sample") %>% mutate(risk_group_pred = risk_group)

#Plot specific survival curves
fit <- survfit(Surv(out_df$V1, out_df$V2) ~ risk_group_pred, data = out_df)
print(fit)

ggsurvplot(fit,
          pval = TRUE,
          risk.table = TRUE, # Add risk table
          risk.table.col = "strata", # Change risk table color by groups
          linetype = "strata", # Change line type by groups
          surv.median.line = "hv", # Specify median survival
          ggtheme = theme_classic(), # Change ggplot2 theme
          palette = "Set1",
          conf.int = TRUE
)

```



```{r}
# Load required packages
library(pec)
library(survival)

# Prepare the test data as a data frame with time and status columns
test_data <- data.frame(time = ysurvtest[,1], status = ysurvtest[,2])

# Get unique death times from the test data
unique_test_times <- sort(unique(ysurvtest[, 1]))

# Check the number of unique times in the test data
n_unique_test_times <- length(unique_test_times)

# Get the unique times from the predictions
unique_times <- predres$unique.death.times

# Print information about unique times
cat("Number of unique test times: ", n_unique_test_times, "\n")
cat("Number of unique predicted times: ", length(unique_times), "\n")

# Ensure that the survival matrix has the correct dimensions
survival_matrix <- predres$survival  # Should be samples x times
cat("Dimensions of survival matrix: ", dim(survival_matrix), "\n")

# Check if the survival matrix dimensions match the expected sizes
if (nrow(survival_matrix) != nrow(test_data) || ncol(survival_matrix) != length(unique_times)) {
  stop("Dimensions of survival matrix do not match the expected number of test samples or unique times.")
}

# Calculate the IBS using pec
ibs_score <- pec::pec(object = list("blockForest" = predres$survival), 
                      formula = Surv(ysurvtest[,1], ysurvtest[,2]) ~ 1, 
                      cens.model = "marginal", 
                      data = test_data,
                      times = unique_test_times,  # Use unique times from the test data
                      exact = TRUE)

# Print IBS score
ibs_score

?pec
```


```{r}
# Load required packages
library(pec)
library(survival)

# Prepare test data with columns for time and status
test_data <- data.frame(time = ysurvtest[, 1], status = ysurvtest[, 2])

# Extract and validate unique death times for prediction times
times <- predres$unique.death.times
survival_matrix <- predres$survival  # Ensure this is in the right dimensions: samples x times

# Adjust the dimensions of `survival_matrix` if necessary
# Confirm the rows correspond to samples and columns correspond to time points

# Specify formula for the survival model
surv_formula <- Surv(time, status) ~ 1

# Ensure times are correct by combining with unique death times if exact = TRUE
test_times <- c(times, unique(test_data$time))  # Merge unique times if exact=TRUE is set

# Run the Integrated Brier Score with `testIBS` parameter
ibs_score <- pec::pec(
  object = list(blockForest = survival_matrix),
  formula = Surv(ysurvtest[, 1], ysurvtest[, 2])~rowSums(predres$chf),
  data = test_data,
  times = test_times,
  exact = TRUE,
  testIBS = TRUE  # Testing IBS at the specified time point # Kaplan-Meier for censoring
)

# Print results
print(ibs_score)
```

```{r}
library(survival)
# Evaluate Brier score at each unique death time
times <- predres$unique.death.times

# Assuming the `pec` package is available
library(pec)
library(survival)
# Prepare data
y_surv <- Surv(ysurvtest[,1], ysurvtest[,2])


ibs_score <- pec::ibs(pec(object = list(blockForest = blockforobj), 
                          formula = y_surv ~ ., 
                          data = data.frame(Xtest), 
                          times = times))

```

```{r}
# Train the blockForest model with importance measure
blockforobj <- blockfor(Xtrain, ysurvtrain, num.trees = 100, replace = TRUE, blocks = block,
                        nsets = 100, num.trees.pre = 50, splitrule = "extratrees", 
                        block.method = "BlockForest", importance = "permutation")

variable_importance <- blockforobj$forest$variable.importance

# Calculate block-wise aggregated importance
aggregate_importance <- sapply(block, function(indices) {
  mean(variable_importance[indices])  # Mean importance of variables in each block
})
names(aggregate_importance) <- paste("Block", 1:length(block), sep="_")
aggregate_importance




blockforobj$forest$
# Retrieve block-wise importance
block_importance <- blockforobj$forest$importance.mode. 


block.importance
block_importance
```
